title: Early Renewal Payment Credit — Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)
content:
**Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** renewals paid well ahead of the term end earn an early-renewal credit.

## Clause

The early-renewal adjustment counts the days from the posting date of the latest payment received for the coming term to the current term end: 30 days or more earn a credit of 4 percent, 10 to 29 days earn a credit of 2 percent, and fewer days, or no payment for the coming term, earn none.

A payment received for the coming term is a payment posted on this policy's premium account for the term that starts on the current term end. Where two entries on a file share the date they are read by, or two policy records answer the same description, the one entered first is read.

## Schedule

| Days from the posting date of that latest payment to the current term end | Adjustment entered (percent) |
|---|---|
| 30 or more | -4, a credit of 4 percent |
| 10 to 29 | -2, a credit of 2 percent |
| 0 to 9, or no payment for the coming term | none |

Every percentage selected for a renewal term is added into one net adjustment percentage, which acts once on the zone-factored layer charge after the elevation multiplier — that charge is multiplied by one plus the net adjustment percentage — and never on the loss-of-use charge.

## Boundaries (hypothetical dates)

For a current term ending on 30 June: a latest payment posted on 31 May is 30 days ahead and earns 4 percent; one posted on 1 June is 29 days ahead and earns 2 percent; one posted on 20 June is 10 days ahead and earns 2 percent; one posted on 21 June is 9 days ahead and earns none. Where a second payment for the coming term is posted later, the later posting date is the one counted.
